title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Hormuz got more dangerous over the weekend: a ship was hit by a projectile on Sunday, a Qatari LNG carrier was attacked on Friday, and Iran says two more tankers hit mines. The cargo forced onto the UAE east coast is now jamming it, with ships waiting more than a week at Khor Fakkan and Fujairah, while tomorrow's US midterms open a new escalation window.

stories.headline: Weekend attacks in Hormuz: ship hit by projectile, Qatari LNG carrier targeted, more mine claims
body: UKMTO said a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, and its master sent a Mayday call. Iran's IRGC Navy said two oil tankers exploded after hitting mines on an 'unauthorized route'. On Friday the Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was attacked in Gulf waters; no crew were hurt.

UKMTO also said a small boat attached two explosive devices to a tanker on 29 October, causing an engine-room fire. CENTCOM says the main lanes remain cleared and has redirected 144 vessels under its blockade of Iran.
stories.soWhat: New since Friday: projectiles and limpet charges, not just mines, and an LNG carrier hit. Gulf war-risk costs will not ease this week; keep sea surcharges in place.

stories.headline: UAE east-coast ports jam: over a week's wait at Khor Fakkan and Fujairah
body: Kuehne+Nagel says container ships wait 7.25 days on average at Khor Fakkan and 8.86 days at Fujairah. At Sharjah the wait is about three days. Moving boxes from Khor Fakkan and Fujairah to Jebel Ali, Sharjah or Abu Dhabi now takes 12–15 days, against about five before.
Some carriers are cutting allocations to these ports, and restrictions remain on foreign cargo and dangerous goods. K+N expects it to get worse and points to Salalah and Duqm as alternatives.
stories.soWhat: The east-coast bypass is now a bottleneck. Quote realistic lead times, charge for storage and detention, and test Salalah or Duqm plus road for urgent cargo.

stories.headline: Khor Fakkan to grow from 3.5 million to 5 million TEU, with 10 million the long-term aim
body: Sharjah plans to lift Khor Fakkan's container capacity from about 3.5 million to five million TEU, and later to 10 million. The port sits outside Hormuz. An Etihad Rail station near Sharjah's University City is due to open on 30 March 2027.
stories.soWhat: The east coast is becoming permanent UAE gateway capacity, not a stopgap. Build a long-term Khor Fakkan trucking and clearance product.

stories.headline: flydubai cancels Riyadh, Dammam and Abha until 5 November
body: flydubai has cancelled all flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Abha up to and including Thursday 5 November, a second slip after the 1 November date. It still flies to Jeddah, Taif, Tabuk, Medina, Al-Qassim and Ha'il. Etihad has cancelled Riyadh and Dammam through 5 November; Emirates plans Riyadh and Dammam from 8 November.
Dubai International is running at full capacity after airspace reopened.
stories.soWhat: New: the Saudi restart slipped again. Keep Riyadh and Dammam express on road at least until 8 November; Jeddah and the west are flyable.

stories.headline: Air cargo spot rates up 5% in a week; Gulf capacity still 19% short
body: WorldACD put global spot rates at $3.80 a kg in week 43 (19–25 October), up 5% on the week and 38% on last year. Capacity from the Arabian Gulf was 19% below late-February levels, and Riyadh was almost closed to international flights.
Middle East and South Asia tonnage fell 6% on the week, mainly due to holidays in India and Sri Lanka.
stories.soWhat: Rates are rising into peak season while Gulf lift stays short. Hold air margins and lock capacity for November and December now.

stories.headline: UAE fuel prices dip for November; diesel down only 5 fils
body: From 1 November, Super 98 is Dh4.16 a litre (from Dh4.40), Special 95 Dh4.04 and E-Plus Dh3.97, all down 24 fils. Diesel falls just 5 fils to Dh4.75.
Brent was $118.07 on 30 October, up 18.7% in a month, so December prices could rise again.
stories.soWhat: Diesel barely moved. Hold the domestic fuel surcharge roughly flat for November; do not cut it in line with petrol.

stories.headline: Warehouse demand shifts to the Northern Emirates and east coast
body: Warehouse renewals rose 21.6% to a record of about 8,200 in the first half, and rents rose another 12.4%, but new contracts fell 51.8% (Cavendish Maxwell). More than 10 million sq ft opened in the Northern Emirates, including 5.2 million in Umm Al Quwain, where rents fell 18.5%.
stories.soWhat: Customers are staying put but stock is moving closer to east-coast ports. Offer contract logistics space in Sharjah, Ajman or UAQ linked to Khor Fakkan arrivals.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Launches dangerous-goods road service across five GCC markets from DWC
body: FedEx now carries dangerous goods by road in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman, under its Regional Economy and Regional Economy Freight services. It runs from its Dubai World Central hub with a GPS-tracked TIR fleet. Eligible goods include healthcare materials, lab reagents, diagnostic samples, dry ice, chemicals and lithium batteries.
competitors.soWhat: FedEx is going after healthcare and battery shippers who cannot fly into KSA. Check our GCC road DG offer and pricing before these accounts move.

competitors.name: J&T Express
competitors.headline: Q3 'other markets' parcels up 159.5%; Middle East named as a growth push
body: J&T handled 104.2 million parcels a day in Q3. Volume outside China and Southeast Asia rose 159.5% to 270.8 million. It says it is chasing cross-border e-commerce in Latin America and the Middle East with TikTok, SHEIN, Temu, Kwai and AliExpress. No Middle East figure was given.
competitors.soWhat: A low-cost parcel giant is scaling fast in new markets tied to Chinese platforms. Expect price pressure on UAE cross-border B2C; compete on speed and GCC reach, not price alone.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Latest result: record Q2 revenue of Dh1.83 billion; Q3 still pending
body: Revenue rose 22% to Dh1.83 billion in Q2 2026 and net profit was Dh47 million. No Q3 results yet.
competitors.soWhat: When Q3 lands, check how much east-coast and KSA road disruption cost us versus surcharge income.

opportunities.title: Oman bypass for urgent cargo
opportunities.text: Khor Fakkan and Fujairah waits exceed a week. Sell Salalah or Duqm plus road into the UAE as a premium lane.

opportunities.title: East-coast storage and drayage
opportunities.text: Transfers to Jebel Ali now take 12–15 days. Offer bonded storage and direct trucking from the east coast.

opportunities.title: Northern Emirates warehousing
opportunities.text: New space in UAQ is 18.5% cheaper and close to east-coast ports. Package it for contract logistics clients.

opportunities.title: Peak-season air pricing
opportunities.text: Spot rates are up 38% on last year and Gulf lift is 19% short. Room to hold margins.

opportunities.title: KSA road while flights stay off
opportunities.text: flydubai and Etihad are off Riyadh and Dammam until 5 November. Road is the reliable product; sell it on fixed terms.

watchouts.title: New attack methods in Hormuz
watchouts.text: Projectiles, limpet charges and mines hit ships this weekend, including a Qatari LNG carrier.

watchouts.title: Post-midterm escalation
watchouts.text: US officials told allies to prepare for strikes after the 3 November midterms. UAE adviser Gargash said the UAE is 'braced for the worst'.

watchouts.title: East-coast congestion worsening
watchouts.text: K+N expects delays to grow; some carriers are cutting allocations to Khor Fakkan, Fujairah and Sharjah.

watchouts.title: Oil back above $118
watchouts.text: Brent rose 18.7% in a month. December fuel prices could jump.

watchouts.title: FedEx in GCC road DG
watchouts.text: FedEx now trucks healthcare and battery shipments across five GCC markets from DWC.

moves.title: Reset east-coast lead times today
moves.text: Update quoted transit for Khor Fakkan and Fujairah arrivals to reflect 7–9 day waits and 12–15 day transfers.

moves.title: Add a congestion and storage charge
moves.text: Pass through east-coast waiting, detention and storage costs rather than absorbing them.

moves.title: Price an Oman-plus-road lane
moves.text: Cost Salalah and Duqm with road into Dubai and offer it to top importers this week.

moves.title: Keep KSA express on road until 8 November
moves.text: Do not switch Riyadh and Dammam back to air until Emirates and flydubai actually fly.

moves.title: Hold the November fuel surcharge
moves.text: Diesel fell only 5 fils. Keep the domestic surcharge roughly flat.

moves.title: Defend healthcare and battery shippers
moves.text: Call top DG and healthcare accounts with our GCC road offer before FedEx does.

moves.title: Lock peak air capacity
moves.text: Secure November–December block space now; rates are rising week on week.
